children.text: This bahay na bato mansion from the 1880s–90s stands in the old center of Angeles. It is a historic site where Aguinaldo's government stayed in 1899, and today it is the Museum of Philippine Social History, open free of charge.

Pamintuan Mansion is a two-story stone-and-timber house in the old center of Angeles City, Pampanga, close to Holy Rosary Church. It is said to have been built by Mariano Pamintuan and Valentina Torres as a wedding gift for their son Florentino, and the National Historical Commission of the Philippines (NHCP) marker says it was built around
. Some sources date it to the 1880s, though, so the exact year varies from source to source.

The house is famous not only for its architecture but for its ties to the early days of Philippine independence. At the start of the Philippine-American War, Generals Venancio Concepcion and Antonio Luna used it as a headquarters, and in late May 1899 Emilio Aguinaldo and his staff stayed here. On June 12 of that year, the first anniversary of the declaration of independence was marked here, and Aguinaldo is said to have waved the flag from the second-floor balcony. For that reason the house is sometimes described as the seat of the First Republic's government. Its use changed greatly afterward. It served as a US Army headquarters, a Japanese military facility during the occupation, a post-war USO building and hotel, a city hall annex, and a regional office of the central bank. The NHCP took it over in June 2010 and restored it, and in 2015 it opened as the
Museum of Philippine Social History
(Museo ng Kasaysayang Panlipunan ng Pilipinas).

Bahay na bato means "stone house," and refers to the traditional homes built by the Filipino upper class during the Spanish colonial period. The ground floor was used for storage or for keeping carriages, while the family lived on the breezier upper floor. This mansion follows that layout, so large windows and long hallways let the air through, and the interior stays cooler than you might expect even at midday. It suits anyone who wants to walk through a Philippine heritage house they have only seen in photos. Angeles is better known for Clark's shopping and nightlife, but the old center has a very different atmosphere. The Pamintuan family was one of the area's leading landowning families, and one of its descendants later served as mayor of Angeles. The mansion is also evidence of how the city grew. If you are spending a few days in Clark, set aside a day to meet the roots of the city here.

It is not a large museum, so an hour or two is enough even at a relaxed pace. It fits well into a Clark and Angeles itinerary as a stop to escape the midday heat, or as part of a half-day walk with Holy Rosary Church and the heritage district streets. Do not expect spectacle. You come for the feel of an old house and a scene from modern Philippine history.

This is the traditional Philippine mansion style, with stone below and timber above. An outdoor staircase, a large door, wide windows and long hallways give a sense of how the old wealthy class lived.

Through the main door, a wide grand staircase leads to the second floor. The balcony where Aguinaldo is said to have waved the flag on Independence Day in June 1899 is the spot where most visitors stop for photos.

Antonio Luna is known to have planned the defense of Pampanga here, and a historical marker records the house as a place where Aguinaldo's government stayed. If you ask the staff, they will often share stories connected to the house.

The galleries are divided by theme: the history of the mansion, Philippine textiles and accessories, weaving tools such as looms, and traditional clothing styles. You do not need long in each one, but the panels are detailed and give a quick overview of Philippine daily life.
A music room plays old recordings, including some from the 1890s, and there is a learning space as well. It helps keep children and students engaged.

A narrow spiral wooden staircase leads up to a tower veranda with a nearly 360-degree view over Angeles. One visitor reported that you could not go up alone and that staff took them up, so ask at the entrance first.

Hand-carved wooden furniture, photos of the Pamintuan family in art nouveau frames, and religious statues are placed in the rooms. They offer a glimpse of daily life in a wealthy landowning family of the 1880s.

blocks.title: A starting point for the heritage district

children.text: Holy Rosary Church, the Angeles Museum in the old town hall, and the Dycaico ancestral house are all within walking distance. Seeing the mansion first and then walking on toward the church is a natural route.

items.title: Half-day heritage district route
items.subtitle: The mansion and a walk around the church

children.text: Arrive at Pamintuan Mansion from your hotel by tricycle or Grab. It is quiet right after opening and the sun is not yet strong.
Sign the guest book at the front desk, climb the grand staircase and tour the second-floor galleries in turn. If you want explanations, ask a staff member to guide you.
Take photos on the second-floor balcony and, if possible, go up to the rooftop tower with a staff member for a view of the town.
Walk to Holy Rosary Church and look around the exterior and the plaza. The church is sometimes under renovation, so check conditions on site.
Finish with an early lunch at a cafe or restaurant around the Dycaico ancestral house across from the church. Check on site whether they are open.
Many sources say the museum is closed on Mondays, so it is safest to plan your visit for Tuesday to Sunday.
Have breakfast near Clark, then head to the old center of Angeles.
Stroll slowly around Pamintuan Mansion and Holy Rosary Church.
Have lunch at a local restaurant in the heritage district or at a mall in town.
Escape the midday heat in a mall or a cafe on the Clark side.
Have dinner in Clark or the Korean town area of Angeles.
Take a direct bus to Angeles from a terminal in Metro Manila. Operators such as Victory Liner and Genbus travel via NLEX and SCTEX, and the trip takes roughly
2–3 hours
depending on traffic.
After getting off at a terminal in Angeles, take a tricycle or Grab to the mansion in the old center. Check the operator's latest announcements for routes, times and fares by departure point.
Highway traffic can be much heavier on Friday evenings and holidays, adding a lot of time.
From Clark International Airport (CRK), Angeles is relatively close by road, and you can get there by taxi, Grab or hotel pickup. Travel time and fares vary by time of day, so check locally.
If you land at Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA) in Manila, the usual way is a bus or chartered vehicle toward NLEX.
Jeepneys and tricycles are common in Angeles. The mansion is within walking distance of Holy Rosary Church, so getting off in front of the church and walking is also convenient.
When using Grab, search the map app for "Pamintuan Mansion" or "Museum of Philippine Social History."
The visit is mostly indoors, so the season matters little, but the dry season is more comfortable if you plan to walk around the rooftop tower or the church.
The morning right after opening is quiet and not hot. At midday the sun is strong and walking around the old center can be tiring.

Hotels are generally found in the Clark area or in central Angeles. The mansion is in the old center, so staying in town keeps transfers short, and if you stay in Clark, spending half the day in the old center works well.

There are reportedly well-reviewed cafes and restaurants around the Dycaico ancestral house across from the church. Pampanga is known as the home of Philippine cooking, so it is a good place to try local dishes such as sisig and buro. Check opening hours and prices before you go.

The mansion alone does not fill a day, so a realistic plan is to see it in the morning and head to Clark's malls or parks in the afternoon. Many Korean travelers make it a day trip from Manila, but the bus alone takes roughly four to five hours round trip, so leave generous room in your schedule.
Visiting hours are generally listed as 8 AM to 4 PM, and many sources say it is closed on Mondays. Check by phone or in NHCP announcements before you go.
Staff at the entrance often ask you to sign a guest book and may offer explanations, so ask for a guide. Hearing the stories makes the house far more interesting.
One report says the rooftop tower cannot be climbed alone and needs a staff escort, so ask at the entrance.
Explanations are mainly in English and Filipino, so do not expect Korean-language guidance. A translation app helps.
One to two hours is enough for the visit. Combine it with a walk around the church and the nearby heritage district.
Follow the on-site rules on indoor photography, and do not touch the exhibits or the old wooden staircases.
On Sunday mornings the area can be crowded because of Mass at the nearby church, so adjust your timing.
Opening hours, fees and closure days change often, so check the latest announcements before visiting.
If you travel with children, focus on the parts they can experience physically, such as the stairs, the balcony and the rooftop tower, rather than reading long exhibit texts.
Whether it is closed on Mondays and whether admission is free differ from source to source, so be sure to check before you visit.
Parts of the building may be closed for renovation or events.
The year of construction and the builders' names differ slightly between sources. Go by the explanation on the marker at the site.
The old-center streets are narrow and busy with motorcycles and tricycles, so take care when crossing.
The stairs are steep and the spiral staircase is narrow, so children and anyone with limited mobility should be careful.
Travel light and watch your phone and wallet when getting around town.
A special economic zone about
20–30 minutes
away by car. With malls, casinos, parks and golf courses, it is a good follow-up after the mansion. Times vary with traffic.
Angeles' main church, within walking distance of the mansion, is known to have been built in 1877. It may be under renovation, so check on site.
A small museum in the old town hall building near the church, reportedly with a separate admission fee. Check whether it is open at the time of your visit.
The capital of Pampanga, about
30–40 minutes
away by car, depending on traffic. A good way to continue with local food and church visits.
